breaking.headline: Chinese shares soar as Beijing pledges state backing
breaking.fact: Chinese shares posted their biggest rise in more than two years on Friday after a State Council meeting clarified that Central Huijin, the state investment arm, should act as a ‘quasi-stabilisation fund’ — the Shanghai Composite rose 3.7% and the STAR 50 surged 15%, while October industrial profits grew 20.1% year on year.

breaking.headline: Brazil’s real rallies as Lula names a banker finance chief
breaking.fact: Brazil’s real strengthened as much as 4.7% to 5.47 per dollar on Friday after President Lula tapped Bradesco chairman Luiz Carlos Trabuco, 75, as his next finance minister, calming markets rattled since Lula’s shock re-election in October; the Bovespa had already jumped 6% on Thursday as the appointment took shape.

watchlist.name: Air Liquide
watchlist.blurb: Air Liquide closed at €191.96 in Paris on Friday, up 0.9% from Thursday's €190.32, as European shares rallied with Wall Street's Black Friday rebound. At the ECB's Nov 27 reference rate of 1.0957 the quote converts to $210.33, just under the year's high of €194.70. Industrial-gas demand stays steady and the CAC 40 is firm; Monday's Paris session sets the next print for the week.

watchlist.name: Anthropic
watchlist.blurb: Anthropic surged 11.0% to $91.88 in Friday's short session, back above its $83 IPO price, as beaten-down AI names bounced after Wednesday's rout. The stock climbed from its $82.79 Wednesday close to lead the AI rebound, with index funds set to add it in December. The Nov 20 Navier-Stokes claim is still unverified, its numerical certificate unreleased — watch for that proof to land or fade.

watchlist.name: SPDR Bloomberg 1-3 Mo T-Bill
watchlist.blurb: BIL ticked up to $91.67 in Friday's shortened session, its distribution yield steady at 4.04% after the $0.30849 payout that went ex Nov 2 and paid Nov 5. The T-bill fund keeps inching higher while a Dec 9 Fed hike looks all but certain, keeping short-term rates elevated. It is the portfolio's quiet cash anchor — no drama by design — while AI names swing several percent a day.

watchlist.name: Alphabet
watchlist.blurb: Alphabet gained 0.7% to $274.96 in Friday's rebound, a modest rise after Wednesday's AI selloff knocked the Nasdaq lower. The stock sits well below its autumn highs while investors weigh new tariff proposals aimed at Asian tech supply chains. Cloud and AI momentum still underpin the story; Monday's full session will show whether the bounce extends or tariff worries take charge again.

watchlist.name: Eli Lilly
watchlist.blurb: Eli Lilly was nearly flat at $1,392.38, up a fraction in Friday's broad rally while holding near record territory. The weight-loss and diabetes franchises keep driving the valuation, with investors watching prescription trends and pipeline news. Lilly has been among the steadier big-cap names through the week's AI-driven swings; the next catalyst is likely a clinical readout or pricing news.

watchlist.name: Cheniere Energy
watchlist.blurb: Cheniere gained 1.0% to $305.04 as energy names joined Friday's rally and natural gas stayed firm heading into winter. LNG export demand remains the long-term driver, with Gulf Coast terminals running hard and new capacity on the way. The stock sits near its highs; watch Henry Hub prices and fresh contracting news for the next leg, and how the Strait of Hormuz disruption ripples through global gas flows.

watchlist.name: Nvidia
watchlist.blurb: Nvidia rose 0.8% to $150.49 in Friday's AI rebound, a quieter session after Wednesday's rout and Monday's surge on Huang's reinstatement. The stock remains far below its highs while the board investigation and SEC probe continue; Huang faces a House appearance Dec 1 and a Senate Banking hearing Dec 3. Sean's call stands: long-term hold until the probes shake out — updates only on smoking guns, not noise.

watchlist.name: Pfizer
watchlist.blurb: Pfizer ticked up 0.2% to $28.52, barely moving in Friday's broad rally as the drugmaker continues its slow grind. The dividend remains the main attraction while investors wait for pipeline readouts to revive growth. Pfizer has lagged the market's AI-led swings in both directions; the next move likely needs a clinical win or a capital-return announcement rather than tape momentum.

watchlist.name: Rocket Lab
watchlist.blurb: Rocket Lab jumped 8.2% to $50.88, leading Friday's rebound as space names rallied with the broader market. The move extends a strong run for the small launcher, with investors focused on launch cadence and the Neutron program's progress. SpaceX's Flight 16 is targeted no earlier than December, keeping space in the headlines; watch for fresh launch or contract news to sustain the momentum.

watchlist.name: Rithm Capital
watchlist.blurb: Rithm Capital rose 0.9% to $9.00 in Friday's rally, continuing its steady climb toward the $9 level. The mortgage REIT's double-digit dividend yield keeps income buyers interested while rates stay high, and a near-certain December Fed hike could reshape the mortgage market for originators and servicers alike. Watch the Fed's Dec 9 decision and any update on Rithm's origination and servicing volumes.

watchlist.name: SpaceX
watchlist.blurb: SpaceX climbed 4.8% to $133.59 as space and AI names rebounded on Black Friday. Starship's Flight 15 wrapped up Nov 14, when Ship 42 was caught by the Starbase tower after a 22-hour orbital flight, though Booster 22 was lost in the Gulf. Next is Flight 16, targeted no earlier than December with Booster 23 and Ship 43, possibly the first Starship launch from Florida's LC-39A. Watch for a firm date.

watchlist.name: Truist Financial
watchlist.blurb: Truist gained 1.3% to $48.50 in Friday's broad rally, tracking the banks higher as the market recovered. The lender benefits from a steepening curve and steady credit, though a December Fed hike is now nearly fully priced. Watch Monday's full session and any fresh economic data for direction; Truist's next company-specific catalyst is likely its investor day or quarterly update.

watchlist.name: U.S. Antimony
watchlist.blurb: U.S. Antimony rose 2.3% to $2.26 in Friday's rebound, bouncing with the small-cap miners after Wednesday's selloff. Antimony remains a critical-mineral story tied to defense demand and China export curbs, with UAMY's domestic supply position the long-term bull case. The stock is still near its lows; watch for fresh DOD or critical-mineral policy news to spark the next leg.

watchlist.name: Uranium Energy
watchlist.blurb: Uranium Energy jumped 5.1% to $5.98 as uranium names joined Friday's rally, with the sector still drawing buyers on the nuclear-expansion story. Term uranium prices sit near record levels and U.S. reactor restarts keep the demand case alive. UEC remains a long-term holding at these levels; watch for fresh utility contracting announcements or government uranium-buying news.

watchlist.name: VI5TC (est.)
watchlist.blurb: VI5TC's estimate climbed 1.6% to $150.00, tracking the S&P 500's Black Friday rally to 7,297.49 in the shortened session. The S&P-anchored estimate moves with the index, and Friday's gain capped the market's best week since April 2025. The estimate refreshes with each index close; Monday's full session will show whether the rally holds into December after the holiday-shortened week.

watchlist.name: Valero Energy
watchlist.blurb: Valero rose 2.0% to $329.39 as refiners rallied with oil's weekly gain, though Brent eased Friday to $94.22. The Jazan refinery attack and the Hormuz tanker incidents keep a risk premium in crude, supporting refining margins. Valero sits near its highs; watch OPEC+'s Sunday meeting on 2027 output targets and any fresh Gulf disruption for the next move, with Monday's full session the next test.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Target 2035
watchlist.blurb: Vanguard Target 2035 held at $28.45, its Nov 25 net asset value, with Friday's NAV still unpublished at the 5 PM build. The target-date fund stays on its glide path toward a 2035 retirement, blending stocks and bonds that grow more conservative each year. It barely notices single-day tape swings; the next print comes with Monday's close, and the fund's mix does the work quietly.

watchlist.name: Schwab Value Advantage MF
watchlist.blurb: SWVXX holds its $1.00 NAV, with Schwab's 7-day SEC yield at 3.79% as published Nov 25, unchanged from the prior reading. The sweep fund keeps doing its quiet job while the market whipsaws around it — the VIX closed at 23.81, down from 26.80 on Wednesday. Per the standing plan, balances above $1,000 get swept into CDs, so the position should keep shrinking steadily toward zero.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Treasury MMF
watchlist.blurb: VUSXX holds its $1.00 NAV, with Vanguard's 7-day SEC yield at 4.01% as published Nov 25, unchanged from the prior reading. The Treasury money fund remains the eTrade cash vehicle, earning more than Schwab's SWVXX while the Fed looks set to hike again on Dec 9, lifting money-market yields further. It is the parking spot for sale proceeds, including the eventual Seiver Slough and Lodge sales.

weekInBrief.headline: Anthropic jumps 11% to $91.88, back above its $83 IPO price
weekInBrief.body: Anthropic surged 10.98% in Friday’s short session to close at $91.88 — its highest close since its Nov. 19 debut and back above the $83 offer price after two sessions below it — as Wedbush, Canaccord and Oppenheimer launched coverage with targets of $120 to $150. Sean holds 66 shares from the IPO allocation.

weekInBrief.headline: Black Friday online sales tracking past $13 billion
weekInBrief.body: Adobe Analytics counted $9.7 billion in U.S. online spending by 6:30 p.m. ET on Black Friday, up 12.8% on a year ago, and expects the full day to land between $13.0 billion and $13.4 billion — above its $12.9 billion September forecast — with Cyber Monday forecast at $15.1 billion.

weekInBrief.headline: Taiwan votes in local elections, Taipei race watched
weekInBrief.body: Taiwan holds local elections on Saturday, with the Taipei mayoral race closely watched: a result read as friendlier to Beijing would ease the political discount on Taiwan’s shares, while the opposite would add to record foreign selling of the island’s stocks.

weekInBrief.headline: Congress returns Nov. 30 with funding expiring Dec. 11
weekInBrief.body: Lawmakers return from the Thanksgiving recess on Monday with government funding set to run out after Dec. 11 and only about two weeks to act; the open question is whether any deal cuts off money for the eight-month Iran war, with Democrats split and Republicans seeking up to $350 billion in new Pentagon money.

weekendStories.headline: KPRC 2 and a motorcycle club feed 30 Houston families
weekendStories.body: KPRC 2 staff traded their usual duties for packing duty this week, joining the Deguello Motorcycle Club and local sponsors to fill Thanksgiving boxes — turkeys, mashed potatoes, macaroni and cheese and sweet potatoes — for 30 families at a Title I elementary school in the Heights. The club, which has helped families in past holidays, hopes to reach 100 families next year: ‘Kindness is free,’ said club secretary Tyler Johnson.

weekendStories.headline: A Sunnyside mom of 11 gets her Thanksgiving miracle
weekendStories.body: Erica Lang, a Houston mother of 11, was brought to tears after losing her food stamps and wondering how she would feed her children for the holidays — until The Queen’s Foundation, a small nonprofit rooted in Sunnyside, arrived at her door with a full Thanksgiving meal. The group is delivering holiday meals to dozens of Southside families and hopes to extend the giving to Christmas dinners.

weekendStories.headline: Bridge The Gaps hits its biggest turkey goal yet: 400
weekendStories.body: Bridge The Gaps reached its largest distribution goal to date at its sixth annual Thanksgiving Turkey Drive at Klein Forest High School, handing out 400 turkeys to Houston families in 90 minutes on Saturday, Nov. 21. More than 120 student volunteers helped — and the nonprofit has now distributed 1,290 turkeys since 2021.

weekendStories.headline: Missoula’s turkey drive sets a record: 1,197 birds
weekendStories.body: Missoula’s 32nd annual Z100 Guerrilla Turkey Drive collected a record 1,197 turkeys and $765 this year — the most ever for the drive — with the Reno Bar in East Missoula bringing in 100 birds and the Missoula Smokejumpers pitching in. The turkeys went to the Missoula Food Bank, the Mineral County Food Bank and four other regional food banks and pantries.

weekendStories.headline: Baraga County shops small today — and launches Baraga County Cash
weekendStories.body: The Baraga County Chamber of Commerce marks Small Business Saturday today, Nov. 28, with an open house and Shop Small Welcome Station at its L’Anse office from 10 a.m. to noon, with refreshments, reusable bags and door prizes. Today also launches Baraga County Cash, a new gift-check program redeemable at any Baraga County business that accepts checks, designed to keep holiday dollars circulating locally.

weekendStories.headline: A Canada lynx comes home to New Mexico
weekendStories.body: A trail camera in Carson National Forest photographed a Canada lynx on June 12 — the first confirmed lynx in New Mexico in about 25 years, confirmed by a New Mexico State University researcher who ruled out a bobcat. The cat lives at the southern edge of where lynx can survive, and the sighting could change how the forest is cared for, since the state was left out of the latest federal lynx habitat plan.

weekendStories.headline: Wolves turn out to be blueberry gardeners
weekendStories.body: Blueberry seeds that pass through a wolf’s gut sprout faster and more often than seeds taken straight from the fruit, a Biology Letters study found: 96% of wolf-passed seeds germinated, against 69% of controls, and half sprouted by day 19 versus day 26. Gray wolves in northern Minnesota’s Voyageurs country eat so many berries in summer — up to 83% of their weekly diet — that they may seed new berry patches far from the parent plants.

weekendStories.headline: A battery-free implant that glows to show it’s working
weekendStories.body: Hong Kong Polytechnic University researchers built the world’s first battery-free, bioresorbable implant that both powers itself and shows its condition from outside the body: it harvests energy from ultrasound and glows under a UV lamp, its outline bright and complete when intact. The device, published in Nature Nanotechnology, could one day monitor patients after surgery, deliver drugs on demand or stimulate nerves — then dissolve away.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: U.S. Central Command said Friday it disabled the Palau-flagged bulk carrier Pacific Archer in the Gulf of Oman, after the ship left Bandar Abbas on Thursday in an attempt to run the blockade; an aircraft struck the stern, knocking out propulsion with the civilian crew unharmed, and CENTCOM says its forces have now redirected 158 ships and disabled six that refused to comply. Mohammad Mokhber, an adviser to Iran's supreme leader, vowed Friday that Tehran will keep the Strait shut while breaking the embargo. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Wednesday that Iran has no oil left at sea to sell outside the blockade, pointing to a Treasury count that fell from about 52.7 million barrels on Aug. 24 to zero by Oct. 22. No Iranian oil is getting past the blockade: Kpler still counts zero Iranian crude loadings since Aug. 24, with about 44 million barrels stuck on tankers inside the Gulf, while roughly 10 to 12 million barrels a day of non-Iranian oil keeps moving through the strait.

comic.title: Tiny Squirrels
comic.alt: It’s actually an open question why squirrels are so rare. Some theories of the vacuum suggest there should be enormous numbers of them at every point in empty space; it’s hard to get the equations to cancel out and produce the observed small number.
comic.credit: xkcd by Randall Munroe — licensed CC BY-NC 2.5; xkcd.com
comic.note: It’s actually an open question why squirrels are so rare. Some theories of the vacuum suggest there should be enormous numbers of them at every point in empty space; it’s hard to get the equations to cancel out and produce the observed small number.

space.headline: Starship gets a two-hour docking test in NASA’s Artemis III plan
space.body: NASA’s mission profile for the 2027 Artemis III Earth-orbit test flight, published Nov. 18, gives SpaceX’s Starship an uncrewed docking test of up to two hours in low Earth orbit, while Blue Origin’s Blue Moon lander test article gets the two-day crewed habitation evaluation. Starship launches from Florida later in the 14-day mission and carries a forward docking adapter; no crew enters the vehicle. Both landers must still complete uncrewed landing demonstrations before astronauts ride either to the surface.

space.headline: ATLAS finds hints of the hidden structure of the vacuum
space.body: The ATLAS collaboration at CERN’s Large Hadron Collider saw more proton collisions with an unusually even spread of particles than expected — a possible first hint of QCD instanton processes, a Standard Model phenomenon never directly observed, in which the structure of empty space itself shapes collisions. The result, posted as a preprint, needs confirmation before it counts as a discovery.

space.headline: A second barrier traps nucleic-acid medicines inside cells
space.body: Hong Kong University researchers found that when a cell’s endolysosomes are damaged, proteins rapidly gather into dense, solid-like condensates that trap antisense oligonucleotide medicines inside — even after the membrane is breached. The Nature Cell Biology finding explains why some promising nucleic-acid drugs never reach their targets, and points drug designers at defeating two barriers, not one.

space.headline: 3D mapping of gene therapy reveals its safety guardrails
space.body: St. Jude scientists mapped 329 integration sites from their X-linked severe combined immunodeficiency gene therapy and found that DNA insulators act as protective walls, limiting effects on nearby genes. The Science Advances findings also fed a machine-learning model that estimates the safety of future integration sites — a step toward safer gene therapies for children born without an immune system.

apod.title: Apollo 17 VIP Site Anaglyph
apod.credit: Gene Cernan, Apollo 17, NASA; Anaglyph by Erik van Meijgaarden — NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day, Nov. 28, 2026
apod.explanation: Get out your red/blue glasses and check out this stereo scene from the Taurus-Littrow valley on the Moon. The color anaglyph shows a detailed 3D view of Apollo 17’s Lunar Rover in the foreground, with the Lunar Module and distant lunar hills behind it. Because the world was going to watch the Lunar Module’s ascent stage liftoff via the rover’s TV camera, this parking place was also known as the VIP Site. In December 1972, Apollo 17 astronauts Eugene Cernan and Harrison Schmitt spent about 75 hours on the Moon, while colleague Ronald Evans orbited overhead.

aiModels.notes: The pick to beat — purpose-built for Spark-class boxes: ~24GB footprint, ~84 tok/s reported, hits the 256K context target.

aiModels.run: vLLM / SGLang / llama.cpp (GGUF); Ollama on Apple silicon only at launch
aiModels.notes: Frontier-class agent scores on vendor benchmarks (SWE-bench Verified 79.2%, unverified); early Spark hands-ons show 40–76 tok/s, but most tokens burn on hidden reasoning.

aiModels.run: vLLM / SGLang (WSL2 on Windows); community GGUF
aiModels.notes: The deep-think option from the project's Nov 20 checkpoint: strongest US-open agentic benchmarks and up-to-1M context, but ~80GB and a Linux/WSL2 serving path.
The turnkey option: maker-documented Ollama path, Apache 2.0, fast on mini hardware (~60 tok/s class) — but 128K context sits exactly at the project floor, and it is text-only.

aiHardware.notes: The frontrunner — the only box ticking every project criterion today: CUDA, Windows-native, Microsoft support, now in stock at the Microsoft Store at the same $5,999. Bolt-class models run ~84 tok/s on this silicon. Ceiling: 128GB is learning-class; it cannot touch Spark Open itself.
Most memory in a mini — room for the 120B deep-think brain plus a fat 256K KV cache. No CUDA (ROCm/Vulkan serving), you assemble it yourself, and batches sell out.

Cheapest US-company route to a 128GB Windows box — on a Black Friday-week sale at $3,999.99 against a $4,799.99 list, so the price may not hold. Launched at $1,999 in Jul 2025; Windows caps its GPU memory at 96GB.

readiness.headline: Close — the box exists and the speed is there; the brain is one tier shy — projected to be at 100% around Q4-2028
readiness.lacking: A local model at hosted-Muse tier (today's best stack is a strong supervised junior) · Spark-Open-class capability needs a ~700GB box — the DGX Station class, whose Windows price is still unannounced · memory-shortage prices are still rising, so waiting keeps earning points · Windows serving paths for the favorite models are proven on paper, not yet hands-on
readiness.today: $5,999 → Surface Dev Box, now in stock, + Bolt 74B always-on (~84 tok/s) + Super 120B for deep think = a working local agent at 76/100. The experience today: about half the capability of hosted Muse — chat at full speed, deep thinking at about half pace. A strong junior on the desk, not a replica.
